seo.title: Hotel Punta Tragara: Le Corbusier Capri Honeymoon (2026)
seo.description: Le Corbusier’s Capri villa above the Faraglioni. Score 83/100, from $800/night. Verdict, suite pick, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Hotel Punta Tragara is the most architecturally distinguished hotel on Capri — a villa originally designed in 1920 by Le Corbusier for Marshall Field of the Chicago department-store dynasty, sitting at the Belvedere di Tragara at the southeastern tip of Capri Town directly above the Faraglioni rocks. Forty-four rooms only — Le Corbusier’s villa was converted to a hotel after Field’s death in 1948, with the original villa interiors largely preserved (the central reception room is the original Le Corbusier rotunda, with the marble fireplace and Cubist murals intact) and a small number of additional rooms added over the years in the same Mediterranean-modernist vocabulary. The site is the genuine selling point: the hotel is built directly on the cliff above the Faraglioni — your terrace looks straight down at the rocks rising out of the sea below, with the natural arch in the middle stack visible from most rooms. Two clifftop swimming pools, the Mammà restaurant (one Michelin star under chef Salvatore La Ragione, serving contemporary Capri cuisine on the panoramic terrace) and the more casual Le Monzù grill complete the food operation. The Belvedere di Tragara walking path from the hotel takes you down to Da Luigi ai Faraglioni and the famous swim platforms in 20 minutes. The honeymoon move is one of the Junior Suites in the original Le Corbusier villa with a Faraglioni-facing terrace, or the spectacular Tragara Suite at the prow of the building. The defining moment: aperitivo on the pool deck at sunset with the Faraglioni rocks below glowing in the last light. Caveats: the 1920 villa heritage means the rooms are smaller than the contemporary Capri Palace or J.K. Place; the location at the Belvedere di Tragara is at the far end of via Tragara, a 12-minute walk from the Piazzetta (mostly uphill on the return); and Mammà’s one Michelin star is excellent but does not approach L’Olivo’s two. But for honeymooners who want the most architecturally significant hotel on Capri with the most direct Faraglioni view, Punta Tragara is the singular choice.
content.best_room: A Junior Suite in the original Le Corbusier villa with a Faraglioni-facing terrace. For the pinnacle, the Tragara Suite at the prow of the building. Avoid the rooms in the rear annex without Faraglioni views — lovely but you miss the entire point of the address.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Belvedere arrival
itinerary_7_nights.description: Sorrento hydrofoil to Marina Grande, funicular up to the Piazzetta, 12-minute walk along via Tragara to the hotel. Welcome champagne in your Faraglioni-facing suite. Aperitivo at the pool. Dinner at Mammà (1 Michelin star).

itinerary_7_nights.title: Da Luigi at the Faraglioni
itinerary_7_nights.description: 20-minute walk down the Belvedere di Tragara path to Da Luigi ai Faraglioni. Sunbeds and lunch. Afternoon swim through the arch. Walk back up. Pool aperitivo. Dinner at Le Monzù grill.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Around the island by boat
itinerary_7_nights.description: Private gozzo boat — Blue Grotto, swim at the White Grotto, lunch at Lido del Faro on the Anacapri cliffs. Return for siesta. Dinner at Mammà.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Capri Town and Villa Jovis
itinerary_7_nights.description: Walk to the Piazzetta (12 min). Early walk to Villa Jovis (45 min). Lunch at La Capannina. Afternoon shopping via Camerelle. Pool sunset. Dinner at Mammà.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Anacapri day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Taxi to Anacapri. Chairlift to Monte Solaro. Lunch at Da Gelsomina. Afternoon at Villa San Michele. Dinner at L’Olivo (2 Michelin stars) at Capri Palace.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Da Paolino lunch
itinerary_7_nights.description: Hotel boat or taxi down to Marina Grande area. Da Paolino lemon-tree lunch. Return up to the hotel via Capri Town. Aperitivo at the pool. Final dinner at Mammà.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Slow departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: Final breakfast on your terrace. 12-min walk to the Piazzetta. Funicular down to Marina Grande.

caveats: 1920 villa heritage means smaller rooms than contemporary Capri Palace or J.K. Place.
Belvedere di Tragara location is 12 min walk from Piazzetta (mostly uphill on return).
Mammà 1 Michelin star is excellent but does not match L’Olivo’s 2.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Among the top Capri honeymoons for architecture and view. The Le Corbusier villa heritage and direct Faraglioni outlook are unique to this address.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May, June, September, October. Closed November to mid-April.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Faraglioni-facing Junior Suites and Tragara Suite 9–12 months for May–September. Standard rooms 6 months.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No, but the 44-room scale and rate mean families are rare. Atmosphere is adult.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: Junior Suite in original villa with Faraglioni terrace. Tragara Suite for the pinnacle. Avoid rear-annex no-view rooms.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Naples (NAP). Sorrento hydrofoil to Marina Grande (25 min), funicular to Piazzetta (4 min), 12 min walk along via Tragara. Hotel porters meet at Marina Grande.
